chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal and Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Ishaq Al-Sha'iri, from Yazeed ibn Kalthama, from Abu Abdillah or from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

You say: 'I have become, by Allah, a believer upon the religion of Muhammad and his Sunnah, and the religion of Ali and his Sunnah, and the religion of the Successors and their Sunnah. I believe in their secrets and their public matters, and their seen and their unseen. And I seek Refuge with Allah from what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and Ali (peace be upon him) and the Successors sought Refuge from, and I desire for Allah what they desired for Him, and there is no might and no strength except with Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended morning supplication to affirm faith in the Prophet and the Imams?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication encapsulates the Shia doctrine of 'Tawalli' (loyalty) by explicitly linking the believer's faith to the continuous lineage of the Prophet, Ali, and the Twelve Imams. It serves as a daily reaffirmation of adherence to their specific Sunnah and theological insights, both manifest and hidden, while seeking divine protection through the intercessory model established by the Ahl al-Bayt. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the Imams as the living interpreters of the Quran and the path to salvation.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hajjal and Bakr Bin Muhammad, from Abu Is’haq Al Shaeery, from Yazeed Bin Kalsamat, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, or from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When you wake up in the morning, do so as a believer in Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, upon the Religion of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and his<sup>saww</sup> Sunnah, and the Religion of Ali<sup>asws</sup> and his<sup>asws</sup> Sunnah, and the Religion of the successors<sup>asws</sup> and their<sup>asws</sup> Sunnah. Believe in their<sup>asws</sup> secrets, and their public (matters), and their seen (matters) and their unseen, and seek Refuge with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from whatever Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> sought Refuge from, and (so did) Ali<sup>asws</sup>, and the successors<sup>asws</sup>, and desire to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding whatever they<sup>asws</sup> desired to Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and there is neither Might nor Strength except with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hajjal and Bakr ibn Muhammad from abu Ishaq al-Sha’Iri from Yazid ibn Kalthamah from abu ‘Abd Allah or abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “

In the morning say, ‘This morning I believe in Allah in the religion of Muhammad and his tradition, Sunnah , the religion of Ali and his tradition, the religion of the successors (of the Holy Prophet from his family) and their tradition. I believe in their secrets and that which is public of them, those present of them as well as those absent. I seek refuge before Allah from everything against which the Messenger of Allah, Ali and the successors (of the Holy Prophet from his family) sought refuge. I am interested in everything that was of interest to them. There are no means and no power without the help of Allah.’”
